detail.text: Two consumer-facing edges of the §6.1 slice, both found by using the store as an ARCHIVE (importing 200 existing sessions) rather than as a live session writer. (1) `WriteTxn::ensure_session(session_id, source, model)` takes no timestamp, and the adapter's `ensure_session` accepts exactly the same three params (src/bin/session_adapter.rs:144-160), so every imported session is stamped with the import wall-clock: the corpus carried `started_at: 1760900000.0` and the store returned `started_at=1792510163.87` for all 200 sessions, with `ended_at` likewise. A session's `started_at` can therefore postdate the timestamps of its own messages (message ts=1760900000 vs session started_at=1792510163 — observed in the same read-back), and since upstream bounds time-window routes on `sessions.started_at` (specs/persistence-shim.md §2.3 `idx_sessions_effective_activity`, §2.4 after_ts/before_ts) any date-filtered or activity-ordered query over an imported archive is meaningless. (2) `record_model_usage` writes the per-model rollup and folds the delta into the session projection correctly (observed 7526/512/10/0.0001 -> 7637/734/12/0.0124 for a +111 in / +222 out / +2 calls / +0.0123 cost delta), but neither `ReadTxn` nor the adapter exposes any method that returns `session_model_usage` rows — the repo's own test reads them with raw rusqlite SQL (tests/hrs109_batch_append_and_model_usage.rs:51), so a consumer building a cost report must know the table and its columns itself. specs/persistence-shim.md §6.1 lists `ensure_session(id, source, …)` and only the `record_model_usage` upsert, so neither is a spec violation; the gap is that nothing a consumer reads (README, skills/hermes-rs-usage/SKILL.md, the spec's §6.2 'what this slice does not do') says so. Fix direction (docs-first, this is a contract/documentation gap): state in specs/persistence-shim.md §6.2 and in the usage skill that (a) session time columns are set by the store, not the caller, so imports carry import-time values and must not be relied on for time-range queries, and (b) the usage rollup is write-only through the boundary and is read with SQL against the named table/columns; if the project decides importers are in scope, add an optional explicit-time form to `ensure_session` behind the same engine-neutral API. Acceptance criteria: both facts are documented where a consumer looks, with the table/columns spelled out; a test or doc-check asserts the documented column list matches the DDL; no behaviour change on the default path.

reasoning: The slice's own spec calls it a 'live session store' slice, and the documented examples all write a session as it happens — so the archive use case is out of the tested envelope, and a real user (this lane) walked straight into it. Unsettable times are the difference between 'my archive is a queryable state.db' and 'my archive has plausible-looking, wrong timestamps'; because the columns look populated, nothing warns the user. The usage rollup's read gap is smaller but identical in kind: the write side is proven, the read side exists only outside the boundary. Both are cheap to close as documentation, which is why the row asks for docs first and a code form only if the project wants importers in scope.
